# Deferral Ledger

One line per deferral. Never close a task silently with a forward reference —
record what landed, what was deferred, and where to resume.

The `status` column tracks consumption of each deferral by milestone **M0119**
(see `docs/milestones/0119-deferral-ledger-backlog-consumption.md`). Values:
`-` = open / 未対応 (not yet consumed); `resolved` = the deferred scope has since
landed (by a later ledger row, a promotion, or current code) and has been
verified by an M0119 triage/consumption task. M0119 sets these values; appending
a new deferral row uses `-`.

| status | date | task-id | landed | deferred | resume point | why |

| - | 2026-09-07 | aio-adapter-lost-checksumfile | **Live defect at HEAD, found and FIXED while triaging E-19's checksum concern** (`internal/initdb/open.go`, `aioFileAdapter.PrepareWrite` / `VerifyRead` + `internal/initdb/aio_checksum_adapter_test.go`). The `io_uring` method's raw-fd fast path hands the kernel a pointer straight into the caller's buffer and never calls `ReadAt`/`WriteAt` &mdash; which is where `relFile` stamps and verifies data checksums (`smgr.go:804-808` read, `:821-823` write). `aio.ChecksumFile` is the hook the method offers instead (`method_iouring_linux.go:391` `PrepareWrite` for writes, `:591-592` `VerifyRead` for reads), and it type-asserts on `op.File` &mdash; which is `aioFileAdapter`, NOT the `relFile` underneath. The adapter implemented only `ReadAt`/`WriteAt`/`Fd`, so the assertion failed and **both hooks were silently skipped**. Consequence on any cluster running `io_method = io_uring` (a live, selectable GUC value, `defaults.go:683` `EnumOptions`, constructing the real method when the kernel probe succeeds, `aio.go:449-468`) with data checksums enabled: every `FlushAllPaced` / checkpointer write through `Manager.WriteBlockAIO` (live caller at `bufpool.go:2635`) landed on disk with **no checksum stamped**, which the next `ReadAt` then reports as a `ChecksumError` &mdash; a self-inflicted corruption report; and the read side skipped verification entirely. Note the adapter's own `Fd()` is what selects the raw-fd path, so the adapter simultaneously enabled the fast path and disabled its safety hook. Fix forwards both hooks conditionally, so a wrapped file WITHOUT them (plain `*os.File`, in-memory test file) keeps exactly its current no-checksum behaviour. Two tests; both FAIL at HEAD without the fix (verified by stashing it) | nothing from this row &mdash; the fix is complete for the adapter. What is NOT covered: no end-to-end `io_method = io_uring` gate exists anywhere in the tree, which is why a shipped write-path checksum hole survived. Every values suite, the pgbench smoke and both bench corpora run at the default `io_method = worker`, whose `ReadAt`/`WriteAt` path checksums correctly, so **no existing gate can observe any io_uring-only regression** | resume = add an `io_method = io_uring` arm to at least one durability/checksum gate (kernel-probe-skipped when unavailable), and audit the remaining `aio.Op.File` wrappers for the same interface-erasure pattern: any adapter that adds `Fd()` (selecting the raw-fd path) MUST also forward `ChecksumFile`, and Go's structural typing gives no compile-time signal when it does not | found while establishing whether E-19's proposed `StartRead` would drop checksum verification. It does NOT &mdash; the source review's finding on that point was WRONG, because `relFile.ReadAt` verifies (`smgr.go:804-808`) and the `sync`/`worker` methods both go through it, so `PrefetchBlock` is checksum-safe on the default `io_method`. Chasing that refutation to its end is what exposed the io_uring adapter hole, which is the same class one layer down and already shipped. Fixed as its own commit rather than folded into a prefetch change, where it would have been invisible |

| x | 2026-09-07 | c19-baserel-scan-priced-on-output-rows | THE base-rel Gather crossover, diagnosed to the mechanism and pinned. `select * from lineitem where l_extendedprice > 90000` gets `Gather -> Parallel Seq Scan` from vanilla PG 18.3 and a bare `Seq Scan` from goopg once the post-pass stands down; `GOOPG_GATHER_PATHS=all` does not rescue it. The parallel terms are all EXONERATED — `cost_gather`, `cost_gather_merge`, `get_parallel_divisor` and `add_path` are faithful transcriptions, and `getParallelDivisor` divides only the CPU run cost exactly as `get_parallel_divisor` does. The defect is in the SCAN's cost INPUTS: PG's `cost_seqscan` charges `(cpu_tuple_cost + qual) x baserel->tuples` (every tuple SCANNED, and that is the term the divisor divides) while `cost_gather` charges `parallel_tuple_cost x baserel->rows` (only the survivors CROSSING) — two different numbers, so a selective scan has a crossover. goopg prices the base-rel scan on the POST-restriction row count for BOTH terms and on a page count derived from that same number, so `gather - serial = parallel_setup_cost + (parallel_tuple_cost - per_tuple_cpu x (1 - 1/divisor)) x rows` = 1000 + 0.0906 x rows at the shipped constants: strictly positive at EVERY row count and EVERY selectivity, so no measurement of the `all` mode can find a crossover that does not exist. Pinned both ways in `internal/optimizer/gatherpaths_crossover_test.go`: `TestBaseRelGatherCannotWinAtAnySelectivity` (the defect, driven through the production producers, asserting the closed form) and `TestPGShapedScanInputsRestoreTheGatherCrossover` (the SAME constants on PG's inputs cross at ~3% selectivity). Corrects C-19d DESIGN 5.1, TODO_ALL C-19h and the `joinpathsparallel.go` header, all three of which state the 0.1-vs-0.0075 arithmetic as a general fact and infer that PG escapes it only by putting joins below the Gather | THE FIX: unifying the base-rel scan onto `rel->pages` / `rel->tuples`. Two sites, both already carrying a comment that names the split — `joinsearch.go:440` (`p.Cost = costSeqscan(cp, estScanPages(rows, width), rows, 0)` with rows = `baseRelInfo.filteredRows`, the serial prebuilt base path the live search actually compares against) and `considerparallel.go:567` (`estScanPages(rel.Rows, rel.Width)`, the partial twin, deliberately priced on the serial one's inputs so the two stay comparable; its WORKER COUNT already reads the real `baseRelPages`). `numQualOps` is 0 at both, a second divergence from `cost_seqscan` in the same expression | resume: change both sites to `costSeqscan(cp, baseRelPages(tbl, baseRows), baseRows, numQualOps)` / `costParallelSeqscan(..., rel.Rows, ...)` keeping `Path.Rows = rel.Rows`, with `baseRows` from `s.relInfos[i].baseRows` and the table from `s.relInfos[i].table` (both already in scope at each site). PG reference `cost_seqscan` postgres/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c:295-356. It is a WHOLE-PLANNER recalibration, not a parallel change: a 0.1%-selective `lineitem` scan goes 161 -> 160,946 cost units, which moves every join cost above it, so it needs its own TPC-H digest + timing table and TPC-DS SF0.5 sweep and cannot ride C-19h's campaign. Expect it to correct a systematic seq-scan preference — a selective seq scan is currently priced ~1000x under its index rivals, which read `relpages` | filed rather than attempted: the owner ruling of 2026-09-07 adopts PG 18.3's parallel cost model as-is, which makes this the mandated direction, but landing it inside the C-19h slice would have made a parity fix and a planner-wide recalibration one unmeasurable commit. C-19h's aggregate case stays landable; the NON-AGGREGATE root is blocked on this row, and TPC-H cannot see that root at all (all 22 queries aggregate at the top), which is why the 22-query census read 12/22-both-ways and looked complete **RESOLVED 2026-09-07.** Both sites are unified onto one resolver, `baseSeqScanCostInputs` (joinsearch.go): a base-table `*SeqScan` leaf is priced on `baseRelPages(tbl, baseRows)` / `baseRows` with the local filter's conjuncts charged per SCANNED tuple, while `addPartialSeqScanPath` keeps `rel.Rows` for what CROSSES the Gather &mdash; PG's two row counts. Every other leaf class (index leaf, subquery, CTE, VALUES) keeps the legacy pricing: an index leaf is the rule-based planner's own choice standing in for the relation and must not be repriced as a full sequential scan. The crossover now EXISTS through the production producers &mdash; `TestBaseRelGatherCannotWinAtAnySelectivity` is INVERTED into `TestBaseRelGatherCrossesOverOnASelectiveScan`, which drives `buildInitialRels` + `addBaseRelPartialPaths` over a `lineitem`-shaped rel and pins the Gather losing at sel 1.0/0.5 and winning at 0.01/0.001. **Measured, TPC-H SF=1, private clone of the bench cluster on :5540, one binary per arm off 71ab15850:** digest 24/24 MATCH on VALUES; plan SHAPE moves on 4 of 22 queries (Q7, Q8, Q9, Q16), the other 17 move on cost only; suite total 144.00s -> 144.13s (x1.001) against an A/A noise floor of x1.044 total and x0.81..x1.61 per query. The one real mover is **Q9, 12.6s -> 18.6s (x1.47, medians of 5 fresh-server runs each)** &mdash; and its new plan is the one PG 18.3 emits: `Parallel Seq Scan on orders` probing a hash of the lineitem/partsupp/part side, `Hash Cond: (orders.o_orderkey = lineitem.l_orderkey)`, exactly upstream's `Parallel Hash Join` shape on :65432. goopg has no Parallel Hash, so each worker rebuilds the whole inner &mdash; the regression is an EXECUTOR gap the parity-correct plan exposes, not a planner error. Q7/Q8/Q16 move the other way (index-scan and IOS leaves lose to seq scans that now read real `relpages`). New pin `plan_snapshots/c19h-baserel-scan-pgpages-20260907.txt`, verified in MODE=costs and MODE=structural. **The direction of the cost move is the opposite of the one this row predicted:** goopg's `tupleWidth` over-estimates (lineitem width=550 vs PG's 137), so `estScanPages(rows, width)` was inflating page counts on UNFILTERED scans &mdash; lineitem 407 529 pages -> 136 393 real, orders 97 273 -> 43 435 cost units. The 161 -> 160 946 rise is real for a 0.1%-selective scan; the net effect on TPC-H is that seq scans got CHEAPER, not dearer, and the systematic bias it corrects is against index rivals, as predicted. |
